title: Evaluation Under Context-Dependent Value: Coverage, Scarce Confirmation, and the Screening-Confirmation Firewall
summary: Evaluation systems often screen candidates before the conditions in which those candidates will succeed are known. When screening and downstream matching are separated, channel-marginal scoring can reject candidates whose value would become high after later information reveals where they fit. This paper studies the design of such staged systems. Blackwell’s comparison of experiments implies that more informative downstream signals weakly increase both attainable continuation value and the welfare hidden by an upstream marginal screen.
